idiom_name: visitor protocol with a default case + element extension via an intermediate base + operation extension via visitor subclassing (virtualized recursion)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the visitor protocol one extra method standing for 'any element kind I do not know', and let the base element's accept hook call it, so a visitor written before an element kind existed still has a landing place. Extend the element side by introducing an intermediate base type that identifies the extended visitor protocol - its accept hooks take the extended protocol and overload rather than override accept - and route the new kinds to the new methods; extend the operation side by subclassing an existing visitor implementation, overriding the default case to re-dispatch to the extended protocol while the inherited cases stay untouched. Whenever an operation creates a visitor during traversal, obtain it from an overridable factory method so a subclass's replacement is used at every depth, and keep the runtime type test that reaches the extended protocol in exactly one place - the dispatch path.
code_sketch:
protocol V1:  visit(Element e) -> default case;  visit(Circle c) -> ...
protocol V2 extends V1:  visit(Union u)          # new element kind only
element Element:  accept(V1 v) -> v.visit(this)   # base: lands in the default case
element Extended: accept(V2 v) -> v.visit(this)   # overload: reaches the new method
# operation extension: subclass the concrete visitor, keep the inherited cases
visitor UnionArea extends Area:
    visit(Element e): if is Extended(e): Extended(e).accept(this) else super.visit(e)
    visit(Union u):   ...                          # recursion through a virtual factory
pitfalls: The default case is both the pattern's safety valve and its trap: an empty default silently ignores kinds the visitor predates, so make it throw unless a no-op is genuinely correct for every future kind.
The runtime type test is the only thing between a re-dispatch and an unchecked cast; keep it in the dispatch path, never in operation code.
A visitor that constructs its own concrete type during recursion silently drops every subclass's extension one level down - route all self-construction through a virtual factory.
